name: 10k-slo-contract

scope.workload: synthetic single-turn, 10,240 requested input tokens, 1024-token output ceiling

design_principle.statement: Data-quality gates and performance thresholds are different kinds of statement and must not be derived the same way.
design_principle.explanation: A data-quality gate asks whether the measurement can be trusted. It can be defined now from measurement properties alone, and it is objective: a run that truncated 40% of its responses has censored latency whatever the endpoint's speed. A performance threshold asks whether the endpoint is good enough, which is a business requirement that the benchmark cannot invent for itself. Deriving a performance threshold from the same run that is being judged makes the verdict circular, which is the same error this project already corrected once in token sizing.
design_principle.consequence: While any performance threshold below is `null`, the strongest available verdict is `inconclusive`.

data_quality_gates.rationale: Gates constrain evidence needed for the stated workload. They do not convert genuine endpoint errors into missing evidence. The sample floor is a conservative minimum, not proof of adequate tail precision.

gates.reason: Any ceiling censoring prevents treating the unadjusted sample mean or percentiles as natural completion latency. Time-to-termination and TTFT remain observations. No survival-analysis estimator is implemented.
An unmatched attempt means an unaccounted request, a hidden retry, or a warmup, any of which invalidates the sample.
If the provider did not see the requested workload size, throughput denominators are wrong. Screening measured 1.16-3.99%, comfortably inside the 10% profile tolerance.

Provider accounting requires observed provider usage and verified provider-versus-target conformance, with independent client counts absent and client agreement explicitly not_observed. Client accounting requires observed independent counts and verified client-versus-provider agreement. Neither mode may back-fill independent counts. Provider mode cannot qualify tokenizer equivalence.
An unvalidated engine schema means the numbers were never checked against the pinned version.
Without raw evidence there is no HTTP status, no finish_reason, and no cache-write count, so success and censoring cannot be established.
Below 30 samples a percentile claim is not supported. This gate degrades the verdict's statistics rather than invalidating the run: the mean stays usable.

performance_thresholds.statement: Every threshold below is null because no operator has supplied a requirement. A benchmark must not set its own pass mark and then announce that it passed it.
ratification_options: Operator supplies a business SLO directly, for example from a latency budget in a product requirement.
A disjoint calibration window is designated before qualification data is examined, and thresholds are set from it. The calibration windows must not be reused as qualification evidence.

objectives.note: Screening reference is the corrected single-window cell MEAN, not a p50 and not a target. No p50 was ever computed: 20 samples is below the percentile floor. The value is here only to show the order of magnitude a threshold would have to accommodate.
Screening cells had 20 samples, below the percentile floor, so no p95 was ever computed. No reference value exists and none is invented here.

No screening reference exists: 20 samples per cell is below the percentile floor, and the C=2 mean is not a p95. C=2 also read lower than C=1 on the screening mean, which is unexplained, so carrying either value forward as a target would encode an anomaly.
Screening reference is the corrected single-window cell MEAN, not a p50, and it is right-censored: it is time to a 256-token ceiling, not time to completion. It cannot be carried forward as a target.

Screening value is the cell mean and it counts reasoning tokens: 87-100% of completion tokens were reasoning. A threshold stated in answer tokens per second would need a visible-output measure that does not yet exist.

Ratify the tolerated error rate before collecting qualification data. Observed attributable endpoint failures are performance outcomes; they do not invalidate evidence merely by exceeding a threshold. Report count, denominator, attribution, and uncertainty separately for each concurrency level. Zero observed errors does not prove a zero population error rate.

ratification_requirements: origin and date of the requirement

precedence.when: any data-quality gate with on_failure=inconclusive fails, or any required performance threshold is null
precedence.meaning: The measurement cannot support a verdict. This is not a soft failure and not a pass.

precedence.when: all data-quality gates pass, all performance thresholds are ratified, and at least one threshold is missed
precedence.meaning: The endpoint did not meet a ratified requirement on trustworthy evidence.

precedence.when: all data-quality gates pass and all ratified performance thresholds are met
precedence.meaning: Narrow claim: this deployment met these thresholds, for this workload, client profile, region and time window.

verdict_logic.current_reason: Performance thresholds are unratified. Provider accounting is permitted for delivered-workload performance with explicit provenance; it cannot support tokenizer-equivalence claims.
verdict_logic.evaluator_note: `src/endpoint_bench/qualification.py` evaluates contract-shaped evidence and is exercised only against synthetic fixtures in `tests/test_qualification.py`. It is not wired to run reports, has produced no live qualification verdict, and cannot change the current reachable state.

aggregation_rules: Evaluate each window's evidence validity separately before pooling anything. A window is the unit of evidence validity.
Pool only eligible per-trial observations from windows with identical workload, client settings, deployment and region. Never pool across data-quality-gate failures.
Never compute a percentile from fewer than 30 pooled samples. The floor is a guardrail, not proof of tail precision.
Do not average per-window percentiles. Pool the underlying trials and preserve per-window counts, failures and censoring.
Publish per-window values beside every pooled statistic so temporal drift remains visible.
A window that fails a data-quality gate makes the whole condition inconclusive rather than contributing to a pooled average.
A qualification verdict requires at least three evaluation windows per concurrency level; one window never qualifies.
Pilot, calibration and exploratory evidence is excluded from qualification evidence permanently, and cannot be relabelled after thresholds are chosen.
invalidation_rules: A change to deployment key, model revision, region, or base URL invalidates the verdict.
A change to AIPerf version, client profile identity, output ceiling, or workload size invalidates comparability and requires a fresh contract.
A pricing change does not invalidate a performance verdict but does invalidate any cost claim.
Results older than the contract's datestamp cannot be used as evidence for it.

evidence_requirements.rejection_reason: Schema 0.1.0 reports a `sizing_verified` verdict derived from a comparison that was circular under provider accounting, and it has no truncation counter, so it cannot express the censoring this contract depends on.

open_questions: Whether qualification describes the observed pooled sample or infers a population parameter; this determines sample size and uncertainty reporting.
How temporal instability between windows should modify a pooled verdict.
Who ratifies a performance requirement, and what record constitutes ratification.
Whether a visible-answer throughput objective should exist, which needs reasoning tokens separated from content tokens per trial.
Whether the intended requirement is a joint success-within-deadline objective rather than separate latency and error objectives.

direction.statement: Publish measured behavior with scope, validity states, counts and limitations. Qualification stays `inconclusive` because no performance threshold is ratified. Inventing thresholds to exercise the qualification path is prohibited: the pass mark must not come from the measurement it judges.

meaning_of_each_option.operator_requirement: supports a readiness claim once evidence is adequate
meaning_of_each_option.disjoint_calibration: supports an identified regression question only, not fitness for a product
meaning_of_each_option.characterization: describes measured behavior; makes no adequacy claim

evaluation_model.problem_this_resolves: Version 1.0 required three passing windows per concurrency level, set a 30-sample floor for percentiles, and stated p50/p95 objectives, while each window holds 20 requests. A 20-request window cannot support a p50 or p95 objective under this contract's own floor, so as written the requirements were unsatisfiable regardless of endpoint quality.
evaluation_model.performance_evaluation_sample: pooled eligible per-trial observations from all windows at the same concurrency level and identical workload, client configuration, deployment and region
evaluation_model.percentile_min_samples_applies_to: the pooled evaluation sample, not an individual window

window_role.evidence_validity: every data-quality gate is evaluated per window
window_role.temporal_stability: per-window statistics are published so drift between windows is visible

evaluation_model.passing_window_definition: a window passes when all data-quality gates pass. Passing is a statement about evidence, never about performance.
evaluation_model.bad_window_effect: the whole concurrency condition is inconclusive; a failing window is not averaged away
prohibited: averaging per-window percentiles to obtain a pooled percentile
evaluating a percentile objective on a single 20-request window
lowering the 30-sample floor so an existing plan passes
choosing pooling or per-window semantics after seeing results
evaluation_model.consequence_for_the_prepared_plan: Six windows provide 120 pooled observations per level, above the 30-sample floor. Four evaluation windows would provide 80. The per-window count stays a validity unit, not a performance unit.
unresolved: whether qualification means descriptive compliance over the observed pooled sample or inference about a population; sample sizes and uncertainty rules follow from that choice
how per-window temporal instability should affect a pooled verdict

calibration_use_case.question_it_answers: has this endpoint degraded relative to a frozen baseline?
calibration_use_case.question_it_cannot_answer: is this endpoint fit for a product requirement?
requirements_before_use: state the derivation and tolerance rationale
declare the calibration windows and exclude them from evaluation evidence
calibration_use_case.note: Independent calibration is not inherently circular: it answers a regression question, which is narrower than product readiness. Multiplying a measured p95 by a constant and rounding does not supply product justification.

conditional_latency_reporting.rule: Publish latency conditioned on an explicitly stated eligible response population, alongside endpoint error count, rate, attribution and denominator, per window and concurrency level.
prohibited: treating a non-zero endpoint error rate as automatic evidence invalidation
presenting a latency statistic computed over successful responses as an overall service claim
conditional_latency_reporting.scope_must_be_derived: derive the eligible population from actual per-trial records; do not assume the engine summary count equals successful_trials. TTFT observed before a later stream failure may have a different eligible population from natural-completion latency.
conditional_latency_reporting.joint_objective_requirement: if the intended requirement is 'requests complete successfully within a deadline', define that joint objective explicitly rather than implying it from a conditional latency statistic
